title: Default DATABASE_URL is a malformed in-memory URI that creates a mis-named on-disk file
evidence: app.py:28 DATABASE_URL default 'sqlite:///file::memory:?cache=shared' produces a real on-disk SQLite file literally named 'file::memory:' in the workspace (verified: `file 'file::memory:'` -> SQLite 3.x database), not an in-memory DB; agent stdout claims 'file-based database by default'
suggestion: Use 'sqlite:///books.db' for the file default, or 'sqlite://' with a StaticPool for true in-memory; avoid the ':memory:' spelling inside a file URI

title: Test reset fixture is a no-op — deletes non-existent 'books.db', leaving shared DB state across tests
evidence: tests/test_app.py:12 reset_db() removes 'books.db' which never exists (actual DB file is 'file::memory:'); autouse fixture therefore does not isolate tests, they share accumulated rows
suggestion: Point reset_db() at the real DB file (or drop/recreate all tables via Base.metadata.drop_all) so each test starts clean

title: Missing-field validation returns 422, not the 400 named in the checklist
evidence: app.py:56-57 BookCreate uses Field(..., min_length=1); FastAPI raises 422 Unprocessable Entity for missing title/author, while REQUIREMENTS.json R9 how_to_verify says 'rejected (400)'
suggestion: Acceptable FastAPI idiom; add a validation_exception_handler mapping to 400 only if strict 400 is required

title: 204 No Content response carries a JSON body
evidence: app.py:159 delete_book returns JSONResponse(status_code=204, content={}) — a 204 must have an empty body; TestClient tolerates it (tests/test_app.py:57 passes)
suggestion: Return Response(status_code=204) with no content, or None

title: Unused import and Pydantic v1 idioms
evidence: app.py:19 imports `validator` (never used); app.py:77 uses `orm_mode` (Pydantic v1 style, deprecated under v2); code_quality=0.79 in scores.json
suggestion: Drop the unused `validator` import; use `from_attributes = True` / `model_config` under Pydantic v2
